preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100) representing the number of operators.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 3 or len(line.split()) == 2 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each subsequent line is either a 'typedef A B' operator (3 tokens) or a 'typeof A' operator (2 tokens).

preconditions.expression: all('typedef' in line.split() or 'typeof' in line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Every operator line starts with either 'typedef' or 'typeof'.

preconditions.expression: all('*' not in token and '&' not in token for token in [line.split()[1] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.split()[0] == 'typedef'])
preconditions.description: In 'typedef A B', the type name B does not contain '*' or '&'.

preconditions.expression: all(len(token) <= 20 and token.islower() and token.isalpha() for token in [line.split()[1] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.split()[0] == 'typedef'] + [line.split()[1] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.split()[0] == 'typeof'])
preconditions.description: All type names (A in 'typeof A' or B in 'typedef A B') are non-empty strings of lowercase Latin letters with length ≤ 20.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout.splitlines()[i] == resolve_typeof(stdin.splitlines()[j]) for i, j in enumerate([k for k, line in enumerate(stdin.splitlines()[1:]) if line.split()[0] == 'typeof']))
postconditions.description: For each 'typeof A' operator at line j, the corresponding line i in stdout must be the resolved type of A, where resolve_typeof(A) is defined as follows: (1) If A is undefined, return 'errtype'. (2) If A is 'void', return 'void'. (3) If A is 'errtype', return 'errtype'. (4) If A is a user-defined type, recursively resolve its definition to a canonical form (void followed by asterisks or errtype). (5) For any type expression, apply the following rules: (a) If the type is '&void', return 'errtype'. (b) If the type is '&errtype', return 'errtype'. (c) If the type is '&T*', return 'T'. (d) If the type is 'T*', return 'T*' where T is resolved recursively. (e) If the type is '&T', return '&' + resolve_typeof(T). (6) After resolving, if the type is 'void' followed by any number of asterisks, return 'void' followed by those asterisks. Otherwise, return 'errtype'.
